title: Sohan Pal Singh v. State of U.P. — excessive bill relegated to Clause 6.5(b)
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Dilip Gupta, J.; Mukhtar Ahmad, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed with liberty to avail Clause 6.5(b).
headnote: A Kutir Jyoti consumer who disputes an electricity bill as highly excessive, including for a disconnection period, cannot have the High Court examine the bill in the first instance. Clause 6.5(b) of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the statutory alternative remedy for a dispute regarding an excessive bill. The writ is dismissed with liberty to avail that remedy.
facts: The petitioner, Sohan Pal Singh, claimed that he had been given an electricity connection under the Union Government's Kutir Jyoti Programme for persons below the poverty line. The Executive Engineer of Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited at Budaun then raised a bill which, according to him, was highly excessive and covered even the period when supply stood disconnected. He disputed the entire bill in a writ petition against the State of Uttar Pradesh and the distribution licensee.

holding_units.holding: Where a consumer disputes an electricity bill as excessive, including charges for a period of disconnection, Clause 6.5(b) of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the statutory alternative remedy. The High Court will not, in the first instance, examine the correctness of the bill. The writ petition is dismissed with liberty to avail that remedy.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the bill, including charges for the disconnection period
not_decided.note: Left to Clause 6.5(b); the Court declined to examine the bill in the first instance.
